history.note: Recorded AT the first commit, not backfilled. `vlhk` is the precedent that makes that worth saying: 54 merges in one window with `beans/workflows/` holding only `.gitkeep`, a STRICT rule whose breach looked exactly like compliance.

Checked for a duplicate first -- `beans create` dedupes on nothing and has produced 14,688 duplicates in this corpus before. Searched the store for `restates`, `bean-restates-skill`, and titles matching restat|drift|copy-of-skill: no existing bean. Created `8v0y` and parented it on epic `1xhc` (CI RELIABILITY), a feature's parent being required to be a milestone or an epic.
Branch claude/bean-restates-skill-gate; issue #1190 opened with the defect, the Jaccard dead end and the scope.

MEASURED BEFORE BUILDING, and it changed the design twice. (1) Three of the four criterion shapes in the specification do not survive the corpus: `## Proposed phases` and `## Rules` occur ZERO times, `invariant` is ordinary prose in all 7 open hits, and a line matching `exit criterion` flags `kn0t` AFTER its repair -- it fails on its own negative fixture. (2) The conjunction is FALSIFIED: the pre-repair `kn0t` references NO skill by path, and the skill existed at that commit (git cat-file -e f8ed0c1a^: confirmed). Requiring the pointer as a condition would have reproduced the Jaccard failure exactly, so it is reported as context that changes the remedy rather than as a condition that changes the verdict. The rule built instead is a phase-contract table: a criterion column that is not an exit-CODE column, over rows enumerating named units of a plan.

`bun run gates`, not a hand-picked subset -- 'a subset of the gate set is not the gate set'. The known pre-existing failure on main (`kg export > a preview says so in its type`, a 5s timeout measured at 5884ms on a clean worktree) is confirmed against main rather than assumed.
